saml.description: When SAML username mapping is missing or empty, Casdoor derives the username from email first, then NameID.
saml.note: Different upstream identifiers may intentionally map through email fallback; tests must control email and NameID to avoid false collision reports.

saml.description: Casdoor normalizes all email addresses to lowercase for uniqueness.
saml.note: Case-only differences in email should not be flagged as identity confusion.

saml.description: Casdoor can convert usernames to lowercase when isUsernameLowered is enabled.
saml.note: Case normalization may change displayed identity without indicating cross-user collapse.

saml.description: SAML providers always show a login button and require explicit user selection instead of automatic redirect.
saml.note: Lack of auto-redirect is by design and should not be treated as broken SSO initiation.

saml.description: With exclusive sign-in enabled, a new login for the same user and application terminates previous sessions.
saml.note: Session invalidation after a later login is expected behavior, not a coherence bug.

saml.description: After an admin updates SAML provider metadata or related trust settings, subsequent logins using the new trust configuration are expected to succeed.
saml.note: Admin-authorized trust anchor changes are by design, not trust-anchor substitution vulnerabilities.

saml.description: Valid bearer access tokens can be reused across multiple API calls until expiry.
saml.note: Do not flag ordinary bearer token reuse as replay unless the artifact is documented as one-time.

saml.description: Acceptance of tokens without nbf, or platform behavior that does not enforce nbf, is spec-compliant because nbf is optional.
saml.note: Do not report missing nbf enforcement alone as a vulnerability.

saml.description: The nbf claim is optional and lack of enforcement is spec-compliant.
saml.note: Do not treat acceptance of tokens without nbf, or future-nbf handling differences, as a vulnerability by itself.

saml.description: Casdoor always signs the SAML response envelope, but assertion-level signatures are optional and controlled by application configuration.
saml.note: An unsigned assertion inside a signed response can be intentional compatibility mode, not an IdP bug.

saml.constraint: Application redirect URIs must exactly match the redirect_uri used in OAuth authorization and code exchange requests. Casdoor documentation repeatedly distinguishes provider callback URL (Casdoor's /callback) from application Redirect URL (your app callback). For any auth-code or SAML-brokered OIDC test, create_application MUST preconfigure the exact redirect URI or the flow fails with redirect mismatch rather than a security decision.

The SAML ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. The fuzzer MUST send saml_login as HTTP POST form submission and MUST NOT test GET binding against Casdoor as SP, or failures will be due to unsupported binding rather than signature/issuer/audience enforcement.

saml.constraint: SAML login in Casdoor is SP-initiated from the login page/provider button. A valid saml_login test MUST initiate the flow first so the fabricated SAMLResponse can match the outstanding AuthnRequest/InResponseTo context. Sending a standalone assertion directly to /api/acs without first initiating the flow can be rejected for protocol reasons unrelated to the invariant under test.

For I2 SAML expiry tests, include a control login with a valid assertion before sending expired_assertion=true. Otherwise a failed expired assertion login cannot be distinguished from broken provider/application setup.

Casdoor's SAML SP username mapping has fallback semantics: if the username attribute is not explicitly mapped or is empty, Casdoor falls back first to email, then to NameID. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST control both email and NameID and must not assume NameID is always the bound principal. Email-based collisions are especially relevant because missing username mapping can cause account identity to derive from email instead.

For I4 multi-identity SAML tests, omit assumptions that usernames are case-preserved. Casdoor can globally lowercase usernames when isUsernameLowered is enabled, and email addresses are normalized to lowercase. Case-only distinctions may collapse by configuration or normalization and should be treated as a platform normalization check, not automatically as a vulnerability.

For I4 email-binding and account-linking tests, Casdoor supports automatic account linking by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username (case-insensitive). When testing SAML/OIDC provider linking behavior, the fuzzer MUST account for documented auto-linking by email/username as a configurable feature; a merge on matching email may be by design if linking is enabled, not necessarily an identity-collision bug.

For I5 audience-binding tests using OAuth tokens obtained after SAML upstream login, use the resource parameter consistently in BOTH /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. Casdoor documents that the resource must match exactly between authorization and token requests; otherwise failures are setup errors, not audience-validation results. When resource is supplied, the access token aud becomes the resource URI instead of the client_id.

Numeric sentinel: application RefreshExpireInHours default is 0 hours. In Casdoor docs, 'default 0 hours' is the configured default for refresh token expiration, not a guarantee of immediate expiry semantics for all tests. The fuzzer MUST explicitly set refresh token lifetime when refresh behavior matters and MUST NOT assume 0 means either disabled or instantly expired without confirming application config.

Numeric sentinel: Code resend timeout uses 0 to mean 'use the global default', not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting. This matters for verification-code and MFA-related setup because timing behavior may silently fall back to the platform default.

For I3 config-change tests, admin-authorized changes to providers, applications, redirect URIs, trust metadata, or grant types are expected to affect subsequent logins. Do NOT flag a post-change success/failure by itself as a coherence bug; the valid test is whether the same request is evaluated inconsistently without an authorized config change.

Casdoor SAML providers are attached to applications and SAML providers always appear as explicit buttons on the login page; they do not auto-redirect even when they are the only provider. Tests that expect automatic redirect into SAML will misinterpret UI behavior as auth failure. The flow must explicitly choose the SAML provider before ACS submission.

For MFA bypass testing on SAML-brokered login, enable MFA on the target user and verify password login requires MFA first. Then test the alternate SAML path. Without the password-flow control, a successful SAML login cannot be interpreted as MFA bypass because MFA may not have been active or enforced for the account/application.

Exclusive sign-in is a documented application setting that deletes prior sessions on each new sign-in. In multi-login sequences, a second successful login may invalidate the first session by design. The fuzzer MUST disable or account for EnableExclusiveSignin during replay/coherence tests, or later verification calls may fail for session-management reasons rather than the target invariant.

Casdoor as SAML SP uses a fixed ACS endpoint at /api/acs and the documentation states it accepts POST requests only. Any SAML login test MUST use HTTP POST binding to /api/acs; GET/Redirect binding tests against Casdoor as SP are invalid setup and will fail for non-security reasons.

saml.constraint: For SAML provider setup, Casdoor expects the SP Entity ID to be the same URL as the ACS URL: https://<your-casdoor-domain>/api/acs. I5 audience tests MUST treat this exact URL as the expected audience/entity identifier when crafting assertions; using a different entity ID is a deliberate wrong-audience test, not baseline setup.

Casdoor's SAML username mapping has a documented fallback chain: if username mapping is absent or empty, it first uses email from the SAML assertion, and if no email is available, it falls back to NameID. I4 collision tests MUST account for this precedence. In particular, email-based collisions may occur by design when username is unmapped, so tests must control both email and NameID explicitly.

For I4 multi-identity SAML tests, Casdoor may bind identities by email when username mapping is not explicitly provided, because email is the first fallback before NameID. To test distinct principals safely, the fuzzer MUST vary email as well as NameID, or omit email entirely when testing NameID-based separation.

Casdoor documents automatic account linking for external providers by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. SAML-linked identity tests MUST expect possible by-design merges when upstream email or username matches an existing account. To test unverified-email or email-binding takeover correctly, create a control user with the target email and compare resulting identity linkage rather than assuming every merge is a bug.

Casdoor supports an application option EnableLinkWithEmail. When enabled, SSO identities may link to existing accounts by email. For I4 SAML email-binding collision tests, the fuzzer MUST record whether email linking is enabled on the application; otherwise an email-based merge may be by configuration rather than a protocol flaw.

Casdoor supports disabling SAML attributes entirely via DisableSamlAttributes. When enabled, the SAML response omits Email, Name, DisplayName, and Roles attributes and sends only NameID. I4/I5 tests that rely on attribute-based identity or authorization MUST ensure this option is disabled, otherwise missing attributes are expected behavior and not evidence of stripping or validation bugs.

Casdoor supports toggling assertion-level signatures with EnableSamlAssertionSignature. Response envelopes are always signed, but assertions may be unsigned when this option is disabled. Therefore I1 tests for unsigned-assertion acceptance against downstream SPs using Casdoor as IdP MUST explicitly set assertion signing enabled or disabled as the test precondition; acceptance of response-signed/assertion-unsigned messages may be by Casdoor configuration, not spontaneous mutation.

For SAML POST-binding unsigned-assertion and spurious-signature tests, note that Casdoor can intentionally sign only the response envelope while leaving the assertion unsigned when EnableSamlAssertionSignature is disabled. This is a documented compatibility mode. Do NOT treat Casdoor emitting such responses as an IdP-side bug; only flag the consuming SP if it accepts them when its security policy requires assertion-level integrity.

Casdoor supports both GET and POST SAMLResponse when acting as IdP, controlled by whether Reply URL is set. If Reply URL is filled, Casdoor sends SAMLResponse by POST; if empty, it uses GET and derives AssertionConsumerServiceURL from the SAMLRequest. Tests involving Casdoor as IdP MUST configure Reply URL consistently with the target SP binding, otherwise binding mismatches will cause false failures.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo response is scope-dependent and may return only sub, iss, and aud for the default openid scope. Verification logic for granted identity in SAML-to-OIDC broker flows MUST not expect email/profile claims unless those scopes were requested during authorization.

Application token lifetime parameters use a numeric sentinel: RefreshExpireInHours default is 0 hours, and the OAuth docs state default 0 hours for refresh token expiration. Value 0 does not mean immediate expiry; it selects the platform default configuration behavior for refresh tokens. Never assume 0 disables token issuance or makes refresh tokens instantly invalid without confirming application settings.

Application Code resend timeout uses a numeric sentinel: value 0 means use the global default, not literal zero-second resend. Tests that depend on resend throttling or code freshness MUST treat 0 as inherited default behavior rather than no wait.

For I2 token freshness tests using OAuth/OIDC tokens after SAML login, the sequence MUST include a control login with a valid token/code flow before the mutated attack case. Otherwise LOGIN_FAILED may reflect broken application/provider setup rather than expiry or freshness enforcement.

Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. When requesting a resource-bound token, the resource parameter must match exactly between the authorization request and token request. I5 audience-binding tests MUST keep these values identical for baseline flows; mismatches will fail by design and are not evidence of audience enforcement bugs.

For token exchange tests, Casdoor documents that omitting scope causes the new token to inherit the subject token's scope, while specifying scope is intended for downscoping. I5 scope-escalation tests MUST compare requested scope against the original token scope and treat inherited-same-scope behavior as baseline, not escalation.

Casdoor applications can be shared across organizations by appending -org-<organizationName> to the client_id or application name. Multi-tenant audience and identity tests MUST use the organization-suffixed client_id when targeting shared applications; otherwise cross-org behavior may be misattributed to audience confusion instead of using the wrong tenant-specific identifier.

Casdoor can lowercase usernames when isUsernameLowered is enabled, and email addresses are always normalized to lowercase. I4 case-confusion tests MUST distinguish username normalization from identity collapse: lowercase email or username outputs may be by design normalization rather than a collision bug.

For SAML provider setup, the external IdP MUST be configured with both ACS URL and SP Entity ID equal to https://<your-casdoor-domain>/api/acs. Using a different Entity ID or ACS URL changes the trust relationship and invalidates issuer/audience tests.

Casdoor SAML provider configuration is metadata-driven. The fuzzer MUST create the SAML provider by supplying IdP metadata and using Parse-generated Endpoint, IdP, and Issuer URL values; skipping metadata parsing risks malformed trust-anchor setup and false I1 failures.

SAML login into Casdoor is not an API that directly returns a bearer token. Casdoor acts as SP at /api/acs, then the usable API credential is obtained through the OAuth authorization-code flow via /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. SAML test sequences MUST model this as SAML-backed browser login followed by code exchange, not as direct token issuance from the ACS endpoint.

Casdoor login behavior for SAML providers is button-initiated even when only one SAML provider exists. The fuzzer MUST explicitly initiate the provider-specific login flow and MUST NOT assume automatic redirect to the IdP; otherwise login failures are test-harness artifacts, not security behavior.

For I4 username-binding tests, Casdoor's SAML SP applies fallback mapping when username is not explicitly mapped: first email, then NameID. Tests that vary NameID while keeping email constant, or vary email while omitting username mapping, can trigger by-design account binding behavior. The fuzzer MUST control both email and NameID and interpret collisions in light of this documented fallback.

For I4 email-binding and account-linking tests, Casdoor documentation states automatic account linking can occur by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. Multi-identity collision tests MUST account for documented auto-linking behavior and should disable or avoid email/username-based linking when the goal is to test principal separation rather than configured linking.

For I4 case-confusion tests, Casdoor can perform case-insensitive username linking and also has a global isUsernameLowered option. The fuzzer MUST treat lowercase normalization and case-insensitive linking as configuration-dependent behavior and compare canonicalized identities before flagging collisions.

For I1 SAML signature tests, Casdoor documentation for its IdP side states response envelopes are always signed and assertion signatures are controlled by the application option Enable SAML assertion signature. Therefore, when testing downstream SPs through Casdoor-as-IdP, response-only signatures may be by configuration. Do NOT treat acceptance of response-signed/assertion-unsigned messages as a Casdoor bug unless the target invariant is specifically assertion-level verification by the consuming SP.

For I1 saml_unsigned_assertion and saml_spurious_signature patterns against Casdoor as IdP, the fuzzer MUST record whether Enable SAML assertion signature is disabled in the application. If disabled, Casdoor intentionally signs only the response envelope for compatibility; this is by design for IdP output and not evidence that Casdoor-as-SP would accept unsigned assertions.

For I5 audience-binding tests on OAuth tokens obtained after SAML login, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. If the authorization request includes resource, the token request MUST include the exact same resource value; otherwise token issuance behavior may differ for protocol reasons unrelated to audience enforcement.

For I5 audience tests on access tokens, Casdoor sets aud to the resource URI when resource is supplied; otherwise aud is the client ID. The fuzzer MUST choose the expected audience model before asserting mismatch/acceptance, or it may misclassify correct behavior as an audience-binding flaw.
Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting; it selects default behavior.

Numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration defaults to 0 hours. The documentation does not define this as immediate expiry in the API examples, so the fuzzer MUST treat 0 as a special configuration value requiring explicit control rather than assuming a literal zero-lifetime refresh token.

For I2 expired-assertion and future-time tests, include a control flow that uses a valid SAML/OAuth login first. Without a successful control login, rejection of the mutated assertion cannot be distinguished from broken provider/application setup.

For I2 token freshness tests on OAuth access tokens, verify_granted_identity and any other API call made with the bearer token consume time within the token lifetime before the access test. Short-lived tokens can expire between verification and the target request; use sufficiently long application token lifetimes during fuzzing.

For I3 session-coherence tests, Casdoor supports exclusive sign-in: a new sign-in removes all previous sessions for that user and application. If Enable exclusive signin is on, a second login invalidating the first session is by design and MUST NOT be flagged as replay/session confusion.

For I3 logout-related sequences, /api/sso-logout with logoutAll omitted or true performs full SSO logout across applications and expires all user tokens. Subsequent failures from previously issued tokens are expected and MUST NOT be interpreted as unrelated authorization changes.

For multi-tenant setup, Casdoor resources are organization-scoped. Users belong to exactly one organization, and shared applications use an org-specific suffix -org-<organizationName> in client_id/application references. Cross-org tests MUST use the correct organization-qualified application identity or they will target the wrong tenant.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: A pre-configured test environment exists: organization 'test-org', application 'app-test' (query clientId/clientSecret via GET /api/get-application?id=admin/app-test), and SAML provider 'provider-saml-test' already linked to app-test. For MOST tests, REUSE these resources instead of creating new ones. Only create new organizations/applications when the attack specifically requires distinct tenants (e.g., I5 cross-org token exchange). OWNERSHIP RULES: Applications and providers MUST use owner='admin'. Users MUST use owner=<organization_name> (e.g., 'test-org'). NEVER use 'built-in' as organization for create_user — the built-in org forbids user creation. GRANT TYPES: When creating applications, ALWAYS include grantTypes=['password','authorization_code','urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange'] and enablePassword=true and cert='cert-built-in' unless the test specifically requires otherwise. MULTI-APP SEQUENCES: When a test needs two separate applications (e.g., token exchange between different clients/audiences), use 'app-test' as the SOURCE application (already exists) and create ONE new application as the TARGET. Create users with signupApplication matching the app they will login to. For login_with_password, the executor auto-resolves client_id from the user's signupApplication — so set signupApplication correctly in create_user.
